text:
maya: quick FYI — we've got several traces that start at the API gateway but then lose span context after the SQS fanout. Dashboard shows orphaned worker spans. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: ugh, yeah. common culprits: trace headers not being copied into message attributes, or they're getting trimmed by an intermediate lambda. are we using W3C traceparent / tracestate?

maya: we should. gateway injects `traceparent` and `tracestate` currently when calling downstream HTTP. for SQS we were relying on 'metadata' blob in the payload, which i think got removed by the fanout lambda that republishes messages to multiple queues.

liam: important distinction: SQS message attributes survive, payload may be rewritten. we should prefer message attributes or a dedicated header field on the SNS->SQS transfer. also watch size limits on attributes.

nina: agreed. opted-in approach: inject `traceparent` and a short `x-redwood-trace` attr with base64(traceparent+json) so we tolerate systems that only copy attributes.

maya: can you share the exact example you used?

nina: sure — when we publish from the gateway we do:```json
MessageAttributes: {
  "traceparent": { DataType: "String", StringValue: "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" },
  "x-rw-trace": { DataType: "String", StringValue: "eyJ0IjoiMDAtNGJmOTJmMzU3N2IzNGRhNmEzY2U5MjlkMGUwZTQ3MzYtMDBmMDY3YWEwYmE5MDJiNy0wMSJ9" }
}```

sam: nice. on the consumer side we need to prefer message attributes over payload parsing. also ensure our OTEL propagator is configured to read W3C from attributes. current OTEL auto-instrumentation expects HTTP headers, not SQS attributes, so we have to add a small shim in the consumer bootstrap.

liam: shim example (node):```js
const attrs = message.MessageAttributes || {};
const headers = {};
if (attrs.traceparent) headers['traceparent'] = attrs.traceparent.StringValue;
if (attrs.tracestate) headers['tracestate'] = attrs.tracestate.StringValue;
propagator.extract(ROOT_CONTEXT, headers, headerGetter);
```

maya: perfect. two related concerns: 1) sampling decision must be preserved so we don't re-sample with different sampling rate in worker. 2) we must avoid creating duplicate root spans in our traces.

nina: sampling decision is encoded in traceparent flags, so preserving traceparent should be enough. duplicate root spans happen when consumers create a new root instead of joining the existing trace — make sure we call `extract` and `startSpan({ kind: consumer })` with parent context, not start a fresh tracer.startActiveSpan without parent.

sam: another edge: SNS fanout with DLQ/Retry lambda sometimes republishes messages with a new MessageId and drops attributes. We should instrument the retry lambda to copy `MessageAttributes` explicitly. I'll open a tiny PR.

ops-bot: deploy queued: fix/sqs-trace-attr-copy -> staging at 2025-03-05T11:22:00Z :gear:

liam: test plan idea: create an integration test that publishes a trace from the gateway using test tracer (deterministic trace id), then assert the worker's received span has that trace id and correct parent id. automate against localstack + ephemeral OTLP collector.

maya: love it. add a negative test for the legacy payload path to ensure we fail noisily (metric) if trace attr missing.

nina: for telemetry retention/exports: we also saw duplicate exported spans when gateway and worker both export the same logical span id (bad instrumentation). make sure only the worker exports the consumer span and the gateway exports the producer span. coordinate span naming.

sam: operational metric: gauge of "trace-context-missing" per queue + ratio of orphan spans. added to console dashboard would be helpful for quick triage.

liam: rollout plan: 1) infra PR to copy message attributes in all SNS/SQS lambdas 2) gateway change to inject attributes (feature flag) 3) consumer agents updated to extract from attrs 4) run integration tests in staging 5) enable flag, monitor metrics for 48h 6) full rollout.

maya: timeline ok? ops-bot scheduled the infra copy patch for tomorrow midnight maintenance window. sam, can you own the consumer shim PR? nina, gateway attr injection?

sam: yep, i'll have a draft PR by EOD and link unit/integration tests.

nina: can do. i'll gate via feature flag and add a console toggle to visualize which queues are flagged.

maya: thanks. one last note: update our OTLP exporter to tag spans with `redwood.queue.name` and `redwood.message.id` so that trace linking + logs query is easier in the console. also ensure sensitive data isn't added.

liam: will add span attributes in the consumer tracer. also add a quick runbook snippet for "lost trace" that points to queue attr mismatch, broken lambda copy, or consumer not extracting.

maya: awesome. marking this resolved for now. i'll follow up with the PR links and a dashboard widget mock. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: note: created ticket INF-8721 "ensure message attributes copied on SNS->SQS lambdas" assigned to infra-team.

maya: thanks infra-bot, closing the loop.
